findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the plan's "budget too short" root cause with scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py's docstring and the 941b correction (the cause was a pre-create deadlock; waiting longer cannot help) before committing a budget-sizing fix.
evidence: Plan: "FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S = 600.0 is an ESTIMATE shorter than GreenHopper's real registration time on this image/runner"

scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py docstring lines 21-50: GreenHopper provisions the fields on first project create, not plugin start; a session-start wait "waits for a thing only the blocked action could produce"
941b comment on ticket 9790: "180 extra seconds of quiet moved nothing... Waiting longer cannot produce them"; tripling the allowance to 1800s (run 30978613228) gave a byte-identical failure
conftest.py:536-542 — the wait is now the ONLY place the fields are awaited, sited AFTER `_create_scratch_project`
findings.finding: The plan's stated root cause — "budget shorter than GreenHopper's real registration time" — is refuted by the code and the ticket record, which establish the real cause was a deadlock (a session-start field wait before any project existed), for which raising the budget provably does nothing.
findings.location: Fix plan "Root cause, confirmed" paragraph and AC lines about sizing the budget
scenarios: An implementer follows the plan, raises the budget, dispatches the harness, and reproduces the identical all-cells-error deadlock because time was never the missing ingredient.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the 'raise the budget' mechanism with the ordering fix the measurement mandates: keep session readiness on serverInfo only, and perform the Epic-field wait AFTER the first Jira Software project is created (the earliest moment the fields can exist), since experiment 30981084637 and the byte-identical 1800s run 30978613228 prove no budget can satisfy a pre-create wait.
evidence: Plan step 2: 'Add MEASURED_FIELD_REGISTRATION_S … and set FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S to >= 2x it.'
Plan Diagnosis: 'The GreenHopper plugin had not finished registering within the 600s budget … The budget is simply wrong for this image on this runner.'

Experiment run 30981084637 (recorded in scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py:14-19 and in 941b's own comment thread): '[before] total=27 customfield_count=0 … [after-180s-quiet] total=27 customfield_count=0 … create project -> HTTP 201 … [after-create+0s] total=55 customfield_count=13 EpicLink=True' — 180s of quiet moved nothing; the create moved everything in 0.0512s.

941b comment 'HYPOTHESIS REJECTED': the 1800s run 30978613228 expired with a BYTE-IDENTICAL 27-field zero-customfield_* inventory after 181 polls, container idle ~29 min after 'Startup is complete' — 'Any budget hypothesis is dead.'
Shipped code conftest.py:178-196: wait_for_jira_dc_ready 'DELIBERATELY DOES NOT READ /rest/api/2/field … that is a DEADLOCK rather than a slow path.'
findings.finding: The plan's central mechanism — keep the Epic-field wait at session start and raise FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S, sized from measured registration time at >=2x — cannot achieve the goal (a green harness) because the failure is an ordering deadlock, not a timing shortfall. GreenHopper provisions Epic Link/Epic Name only when the first Jira Software project is created; the session-start wait blocks the very action that would produce the fields, so no budget can satisfy it.
findings.location: Fix plan (rebar-debug Phase 2), step 2 'Size the budget from the measurement'; Diagnosis section ('READINESS/TIMING, not a genuine degrade … The budget is simply wrong for this image on this runner')
scenarios: Any harness run: the session-start field wait sees a fresh, project-less instance (27 system fields, zero customfield_*), exhausts whatever budget it is given, and errors all 62 cells at setup — exactly as 600s and 1800s both did.
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt the control-flow/ordering alternative: (1) wait_for_jira_dc_ready gates on serverInfo and does NOT read /rest/api/2/field; (2) route the Epic-field await through _assert_project_capabilities, which runs immediately after _create_scratch_project's 201; (3) because provisioning is sub-second post-create (0.0512s measured), set a small bounded budget with a fine poll cadence rather than a large multi-minute one; (4) rewrite not_ready_message so it no longer names 'budget too short' as a cause.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the load-bearing capability assertion against the repo's own prior art before committing: reconcile 'GreenHopper registers custom fields progressively / the budget is too short' with experiment run 30981084637 (fields provisioned in 0.0512s on the first Software project create, unmoved by 180s quiet and by an 1800s budget), and re-diagnose accordingly rather than sizing a larger budget.
evidence: Plan asserts (Fix plan §3): 'Jira registers custom fields progressively, so bailing on that signal would reintroduce the race'; and (Root cause) 'FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S = 600.0 is an ESTIMATE shorter than GreenHopper's real registration time on this image/runner'.

REFUTED by the repo's own recorded measurement: scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py module docstring / PROVISIONING_TO_FIELDS_VISIBLE_S cites experiment run 30981084637 — '[after-180s-quiet] total=27 customfield_count=0 ... create project -> HTTP 201 ... [after-create+0s] total=55 customfield_count=13 EpicLink=True'. Fields are event-provisioned on the first Jira Software project create (0.0512s), NOT time-provisioned.

The current not_ready_message docstring (scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py:288-299) explicitly warns the plan's exact rule is FALSE and self-confirming: the previous wording that 'no customfield_* meant the allowance is too short' is 'FALSE — run 30981084637 held such an instance quiet for 180 extra seconds with zero change' and 'bought a wasted 50-minute run'.

Independent disconfirmation in-repo: run 30978613228 tripled the budget to 1800s and produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL 27-field, zero-customfield failure with the container idle ~29 minutes after 'Startup is complete' — recorded in the module docstring lines 36-39 and the ticket's 'HYPOTHESIS REJECTED' comment.
findings.finding: The plan's load-bearing capability assertion — that GreenHopper 'registers custom fields progressively' over time so a larger measured budget will cure the 62-cell setup errors — is unverified and is directly refuted by prior art the plan does not consult, including the very module it edits.
findings.location: Fix plan (rebar-debug Phase 2) §2–§3 and 'Diagnosis' / 'Why the old gate worked'
scenarios: An operator follows the plan, sets FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S to >=2× a 'measured' number, dispatches the ~50-minute harness, and the run errors all 62 cells again with an unchanged inventory — because the fields never register without a project create, which the session-start wait blocks.

The plan is executed against main, whose live code already relocated the wait to post-project-create (Gerrit 1421); the plan's non-goal 'do NOT change the two-stage shape' plus its budget-raise would re-diverge from the shipped fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Abandon the budget-sizing hypothesis. The measured prior art shows the Epic fields are provisioned by the first Jira Software project create, not by elapsed time, so the correct fix is to move the field wait AFTER _create_scratch_project (into _assert_project_capabilities), as already done in Gerrit 1421 — not to raise FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S. Rewrite the not_ready_message decision rule to stop pointing readers at the budget.

Step 5: 'Dispatch the harness workflow and require 0 failed AND 0 errored cells, recording ... the elapsed registration time it reports.'
ABSENCE: no stated interim budget for the first dispatch that produces the measurement — the number the budget is sized from cannot be observed until the budget already passes.
findings.finding: The measurement bootstrap is circular and under-specified: MEASURED_FIELD_REGISTRATION_S is to be 'recorded verbatim from a live harness run's readiness line' (step 2) and the success-side readiness line only exists after step 1 ships, but a green readiness line can only be produced once the budget is already large enough for the wait to succeed. The plan does not state which initial/interim budget value to run the first measuring dispatch with.
scenarios: Executor ships step 1, dispatches at the current 600s budget, the run errors again (600s < real registration), and no readiness line is ever produced to size the budget from.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit bootstrap step: set a provisional oversized budget, dispatch to obtain the green readiness line, read MEASURED_FIELD_REGISTRATION_S from it, then set FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S to >= 2x that measured value and re-verify.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the multiplier from stage-TWO (field-registration) variance, or state explicitly why stage-one runner spread is a valid proxy for the field-registration budget being sized.
evidence: Step 2: 'stage one of the same gate took 316s on run 30964805133 and 485s on run 30975323866 — a 1.53x runner-to-runner spread on the same image ... so the budget must absorb at least that much variance.'
The budget being sized (FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S) governs the field-registration wait (stage two), not stage one.
findings.finding: Step 2 justifies the 2x multiplier using stage-ONE gate times (316s / 485s), but MEASURED_FIELD_REGISTRATION_S is the field-registration (stage two) measurement — the plan does not establish that stage-one runner-to-runner variance is representative of stage-two variance, so the 2x sizing rests on a possibly-mismatched envelope.
scenarios: Stage-two registration variance exceeds the stage-one-derived 1.53x envelope, so 2x is still short and the harness errors again.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop the stage-one-derived '2x' multiplier justification; with the wait moved post-create, size the small bounded budget from the measured sub-second post-create provisioning time (0.0512s on run 30981084637), not from serverInfo variance.
evidence: Plan step 2 attributes the 1.53x spread to 'stage one of the same gate' (serverInfo), then uses it to size the field-readiness (stage two) budget.
941b Phase-2 comment concedes this in review: 'the 316s/485s figures are stage-ONE (serverInfo) durations, NOT stage-two field registration … label the multiplier a runner-variance PROXY.'
findings.finding: Even granting the (incorrect) budget approach, the plan's justification for the '>=2x' multiplier is unsound: it derives the 2x from 316s vs 485s figures that are STAGE-ONE serverInfo durations, not stage-two Epic-field registration times, so the multiplier is sized from the wrong quantity.
findings.location: Fix plan step 2 ('The 2x is itself measured: stage one of the same gate took 316s on run 30964805133 and 485s on run 30975323866')
scenarios: A budget sized from stage-one variance has no bearing on stage-two registration variance; it could be arbitrarily wrong in either direction.
